text: Where is Lily? On the chair.
goal: Nan lifts a big pink blanket on the big soft armchair in the same living room; Lily (drawn young, about five years old) sits curled up on the chair under the blanket and smiles.
colorPrompt: Compose one children's book picture from the element pictures. Picture 1 shows the girl Nan in a full-body view: copy her exactly. Picture 2 is a close-up of Nan's face with the correct, clean eyes: copy her face and eyes from it exactly; each eye ends in a smooth, rounded outer corner with one short, thick, curved eyelash flick; there is no pale skin flap, no torn edge, and no separate small tick mark at any eye corner. Picture 3 shows the girl Lily, front view and three-quarter view: copy only the girl. Picture 4 is the empty empty cozy living room of Nan: warm cream walls, a light wooden floor, a blue sofa with one cushion and a folded blanket on its arm, a big round soft rug, a wooden toy box with a few toys at the right, and a small window at the left; use it as the background and keep the same room. Picture 5 is a 3D render of ONE small wooden chair with four legs and a low back, on a gray or white background, perhaps with a ground shadow; ignore the background and the shadow, and draw the same object with the same shape and colors. Keep the soft, round, bright 3D render look of the pictures, not a 2D drawing and no outlines. The children keep their chibi proportions: a big head and a small body; Mom keeps the adult proportions of her picture (about one and a half times as tall as a five-year-old child); Tom, who is eight, is a little taller than a five-year-old child and has the same chibi proportions. Hands are small, clean hands with five clear short fingers (four fingers and one thumb) when open, never fists unless stated, and a hanging hand shows relaxed, separate short fingers. Rendering errors to NOT copy from the character pictures: a tiny dark tick mark or pale skin flap at the outer corner of an eye, and a faint pale crease on a forehead. Each eye ends in a smooth, rounded corner; no character here has an eyelash flick. Clean eye corners, no streak on the forehead, no marks on the face. The ears are smooth, with one clean rounded rim. Each piece of clothing is one even color with no pale patches, no pale blotches at the shoulders, and no stains. Do not change anyone's hair or clothes. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no writing on any picture or sign. The picture is for young children and is rated G. Keep each character exactly as in the pictures: Nan: black-brown hair in exactly two round buns with smooth red ring bands (no bun on top), large dark-brown eyes, an orange T-shirt with a white star, red shorts, white sneakers; Lily: a girl of five with a short dark-brown bob with a straight fringe and one small lilac bow at the side of her hair, big brown eyes, a lilac dress with short sleeves and a small white collar, white socks, pink shoes. The picture: Nan lifts a big pink blanket on the big soft armchair in the same living room; Lily (drawn young, about five years old) sits curled up on the chair under the blanket and smiles. Simple objects with no reference picture: ONE big soft armchair. The object counts: exactly ONE chair. A wide shot at a low camera height in the room. Exactly the characters named here are in the picture, and no other person or animal. A character of the pictures that this description does not name must not appear. Every named character has a clear, whole, friendly face. The page text is "Where is Lily? On the chair." and is context only: do not draw any text.
linePrompt: Picture 1 is a 3D-rendered children's book picture. Convert picture 1 to line art for a student book: thick, even black lines (about three times a normal outline), simple closed shapes that a 5-year-old can color, on pure white. No blush circles, no eyelash ticks, no hair strands, no shading, no gray, no texture lines, no text. Keep every shape in the same place and the same size. Draw each eye as a closed outline with a big solid black pupil (a filled black circle) inside it. Draw the mouth exactly as in picture 1: an open mouth stays an open mouth drawn as a closed outline, and a closed smile stays one curve. Draw each hand as a closed outline with each finger as a separate rounded shape. Each head of hair is one closed shape. The ear is one closed outline with at most one inner curve. No lines on the clothes other than the outline, the collar, the cuffs, the buttons, and the pocket. No wrinkle lines on any face. Simplify the background: draw only a few large, simple, closed shapes (the floor line, the wall line, the window as one closed rectangle, the sofa as one closed shape with its cushion as one closed shape, the rug as one closed oval, and the toy box as one closed box shape with its lid). No wood grain lines, no floor plank lines, no wall texture, no hatching, no tick marks, no small details. Every outline is one closed line that never runs into a background line; no loose line ends anywhere. Every line inside an object ends on another line. Use few background shapes. Each eye of every person is a ring: one closed outline circle with a smaller solid black circle inside it and a thin white gap between the two; no eye is a solid black shape without an outline. Mom's wavy hair is one closed cloud-like shape with no strands; her collar, her cuffs, her jeans, and each sneaker are closed shapes. Tom's hair is one closed shape with a side sweep; his T-shirt, shorts, and each shoe are closed shapes. Each hand is one closed outline with five fingers drawn as separate rounded closed shapes (four fingers and one thumb). The top is one closed shape with its yellow stripe as one closed band, its stem and knob as closed shapes, and its point as one closed shape; no motion lines. Pip: the ears, the collar, and the round tag are separate closed shapes; the fur has no strands.
